title: Global sensitivity anova and sobol estimation

items.title: Shapley effects for dependent inputs
items.strategy: Fix the variance game v(S)=Var(E[f|X_S]), state the positive-output-variance convention, and define the normalized average marginal contribution over all input permutations.

items.title: Product-coordinate averaging operators
items.strategy: Define each coordinate-subset averaging operator on a finite product probability law as a section integral; the following in-pair lemma proves representative independence, L2 contraction, projection, commutation, and self-adjointness.

items.title: Sharp Poincare bound for the uniform law on an interval
items.strategy: Reflect the centered function evenly to a periodic absolutely continuous function, derive its Fourier derivative coefficients by integration by parts, and apply Parseval to obtain the sharp constant L^2/pi^2.

items.title: Exact finite-permutation Shapley effects
items.strategy: Enumerate each of the d! permutations, accumulate each input's marginal coalition increment, then divide the averages by the positive total variance.

items.title: Monte Carlo permutation estimator for Shapley effects
items.strategy: Sample a declared number of independent uniform permutations and report the coordinatewise mean marginal contribution and sample-covariance standard errors.

items.title: Product-coordinate projections commute and contract in L2
items.strategy: Apply Tonelli to squared sections and Cauchy-Schwarz to prove L2 contraction; use finite-product Fubini to prove P_J P_K=P_{J intersect K} and self-adjointness.

items.title: Dependent-input Shapley effects are nonnegative and sum to one
items.strategy: Nested conditional-expectation projections make every coalition marginal nonnegative; telescope the marginal increments along each finite permutation to prove efficiency.

items.title: Product-law Hoeffding ANOVA components
items.strategy: Define each component by the finite Möbius sum of the coordinate projections; the projection identities make this a well-defined L2 class.

items.title: Monte Carlo permutation Shapley effects have a joint CLT
items.strategy: The bounded vector of permutation increments is iid; apply the vector strong law, multivariate CLT, and entrywise weak law to its sample covariance.

items.title: Independent product inputs have an orthogonal Hoeffding decomposition
items.strategy: Expand the Möbius sums and use the projection composition identity to prove reconstruction, coordinatewise centering, and pairwise orthogonality; Pythagoras gives the variance sum.

items.title: First-order and total Sobol indices
items.strategy: For positive output variance only, normalize the singleton variance component and the sum of components containing the selected coordinate.

items.title: Complete orthonormal tensor expansions group into Sobol components
items.strategy: For finite sums, Möbius inversion of each product basis tensor retains exactly its coordinate support; pass to a complete countable basis using L2 convergence, projection contraction, and Parseval. The completeness hypothesis remains explicit and law-specific.

items.title: Pick-freeze covariances recover first and total Sobol numerators
items.strategy: Integrate over independent replacement coordinates: the first-order product becomes the squared conditional projection, while half the squared total-freeze difference is the residual variance after averaging over all coordinates except i.

items.title: Coordinate Poincare inequalities bound total Sobol effects
items.strategy: The total-effect numerator is the integrated conditional variance given all other coordinates; apply the one-dimensional Poincare inequality on almost every coordinate slice and integrate.

items.title: Pick-freeze Monte Carlo estimators for Sobol indices
items.strategy: Use independent product-law bundles to form unbiased first-order and total-effect numerators and an independent pair-difference variance denominator; report raw ratios only when the empirical denominator is positive.

items.title: Pick-freeze Sobol ratios are consistent and have a joint delta-method CLT
items.strategy: Finite fourth moments make the joint row vector square-integrable; the strong law gives consistency, the multivariate CLT and differentiability of division by positive variance give the joint limit, and the weak law for products validates plug-in covariance MCSE.

title: Global sensitivity anova and sobol estimation — Examples

items.title: Perfectly correlated inputs share a Shapley effect
items.strategy: For X1=X2=Z and f=Z, compute the two coalition values, enumerate both permutations, and verify equal allocation and efficiency.

items.title: The Ishigami function's only possible interaction is X1-X3
items.strategy: Integrate the sine and polynomial factors under independent uniform laws, isolate the X1-X3 interaction, and compute the exact variance components and indices.

items.title: Polynomial-chaos coefficients group by variable support
items.strategy: Use the complete four-mode tensor basis for two symmetric two-point inputs and an exact finite expansion; verify the coefficient support sums and state the no-completeness boundary for general UQ1 cutoffs.

items.title: A constant output has no normalized Sobol indices
items.strategy: For a constant function, every nonempty ANOVA component and the total variance vanish, so the positive-variance denominator condition fails.

items.title: Noisy simulator output separates intrinsic noise from input variance
items.strategy: For Y=f(X)+epsilon with centered independent noise, factor the covariance, decompose total output variance, and compare conditional-mean and raw-output denominators.

items.title: A pick-freeze ratio can be biased at finite sample size
items.strategy: For a one-factor Bernoulli output and one sample bundle, condition on a positive empirical variance denominator and calculate the ratio expectation explicitly.
